cards.name: Lens Flare
cards.summary: Renders a classic optical lens flare (hot spot, streaks and a chain of coloured ghosts) on top of the layer at a chosen point.
use_for: sun or stage-light glint on a trailer title or hero shot
light sweep across a logo or channel bumper (keyframe Flare Center)
spotlight / live-event feel on a rally or stage shot
flash transition when Brightness is keyframed up then down
avoid: default settings read as a dated stock effect; keep Brightness modest and use Blend With Original
a flare not tied to a real light source in the shot looks fake
8-bit generator; can band on heavy dark grades

params.name: Flare Center
params.does: position of the hot spot in layer pixels; ghosts line up through frame centre
params.typical: on a real light source or near a top corner, e.g. [1550, 180]

params.name: Flare Brightness
params.does: flare intensity / size in %

params.name: Lens Type
params.does: simulated lens: 1 = 50-300mm Zoom (busiest, longest chain of ghosts), 2 = 35mm Prime, 3 = 105mm Prime (fewer ghosts, different halo/streak shape)
params.typical: 1 for a big trailer flare; try 2 or 3 for a simpler flare

params.name: Blend With Original
params.does: mixes back toward the untouched image (100 = no flare)

cards.scripting: Draws directly onto the layer it is applied to (no transparent/composite option). For a flare you can move and blend independently, apply it to a black solid and set that layer's blend mode to Add or Screen. Flare Center is in layer pixels; the default [768,432] sits up-left of centre, so always set it explicitly. Lens Type is a 1-based popup. 8 bpc effect.

verified.note: Bright hot spot with streaks at top right and a chain of coloured ghost rings running down-left across the foreground, image otherwise intact.

cards.name: Paint Bucket
cards.summary: Flood-fills a region of similar colour, starting from the Fill Point, with a solid colour (like Photoshop's paint bucket), with optional feathered, spread, choked or stroke-only edges.
use_for: recolour a flat region of a logo, map or vector graphic
fill outline / line-art illustrations in explainer animations
colour one state or constituency on a flat political map graphic
outline-only highlight of a flat shape region (Stroke = Stroke)
avoid: on live-action footage the fill is blotchy and flickers frame to frame as pixel colours change
high Tolerance floods most of the frame
Fill Point is fixed in layer space; moving subjects slip out of the fill

params.name: Fill Point
params.does: pixel where the flood fill starts (layer pixels)
params.typical: inside the flat region to colour

params.name: Tolerance
params.does: how different a pixel can be from the seed colour and still be filled (0-255)

params.name: Fill Selector
params.does: what is compared when growing the fill (colour+alpha, straight colour, transparency, opacity, alpha)

params.name: Stroke
params.does: edge treatment of the fill
params.typical: 1 Antialias for clean fills, 2 Feather for soft, 5 Stroke for outline only

params.name: Contextual Slider
params.does: amount for the chosen Stroke mode (feather softness, spread/choke radius or stroke width)

params.name: Color
params.does: fill colour

params.name: Opacity
params.does: fill opacity in %

params.name: Blending Mode
params.does: how the fill composites over the layer (1-based popup, 23 slots)

cards.scripting: Fill Point is in layer pixels. Fill Selector (read from After Effects 26.0): 1 Color & Alpha, 2 Straight Color, 3 a separator, 4 Transparency, 5 Opacity, 6 Alpha Channel. Blending Mode: 1 Fill Only, 2 Normal (default), 3 Stencil Alpha, then the layer modes with separators at 4, 11, 14 and 19 (enum_labels). View Threshold = 1 shows a black/white preview of the selection, keep it 0 for renders. No Premiere equivalent: Paint Bucket is absent from the harvested Premiere 2026 video-effect list.

verified.note: A flat pink-red fill flooded out from the centre over most of the frame (figures, stripes, wall), leaving only blotchy islands of the original, as the Tolerance-90 warning predicts.

cards.name: Radio Waves
cards.summary: Generates rings (circles, polygons or stars, or copies of a mask or image contour) that expand outward from a point over time, like sonar or broadcast signal pulses.
use_for: pulsing signal behind a LIVE / Breaking News badge
radar ping on a map location (rally venue, incident site)
rings behind a phone or notification icon in tech explainers
beat-synced shockwave accent in reels
avoid: default thin blue rings look like a 2005 template; set colour, widths and fade
nothing is visible at the very first frame because waves are born over time
large Lifespan with high Frequency piles up hundreds of rings and slows renders

params.name: Producer Point
params.does: centre the waves are emitted from (layer pixels)
params.typical: the map pin or badge position

params.name: Wave Type
params.does: shape source: 1 Polygon (circle/polygon/star), 2 Image Contours, 3 Mask

params.name: Frequency
params.does: waves emitted per second

params.name: Expansion
params.does: how fast each wave grows

params.name: Lifespan (sec)
params.does: how long each wave lives before it disappears (note trailing space in the name)

params.name: Color
params.does: stroke colour

params.name: Start Width
params.does: stroke width at birth

params.name: End Width
params.does: stroke width at end of life

params.name: Fade-out Time
params.does: how long each wave takes to fade out before it dies (seconds, believed); default 5 is longer than a short Lifespan, so rings start part-faded

cards.scripting: The property name 'Lifespan (sec) ' ends with a space; use it exactly. Waves are generated over time from the layer's start, so sample/preview frames at least 1 s in. The effect renders the waves on transparency and hides the layer's own pixels (verified: applied to footage the frame showed only rings on black), so apply it to a full-frame solid above the footage rather than to the footage itself. Image Contours mode needs Source Layer (layer reference, not settable from a spec) and Mask mode needs a mask (mask reference). Opacity is 0-1, not %. Profile: 1 Square, 2 Triangle, 3 Sawtooth Out, 4 Sawtooth In, 5 Gaussian, 6 Bell, 7 Sine (read from After Effects 26.0). Orientation/Direction are angles in degrees; Velocity moves rings along Direction.

verified.note: Six evenly spaced cyan concentric rings around a centre dot on solid black: the waves render and the footage itself is hidden.

cards.name: Scribble
cards.summary: Fills or outlines a mask with animated, hand-drawn-looking zig-zag scribble strokes that can wiggle and draw on over time.
use_for: hand-scribbled highlight or redaction over a word or face mask in explainers
doodle-style draw-on of shapes in reels
marker-style fills for infographic bars or map regions
cross-out / scribble-over a claim in fact-check videos
avoid: without a mask nothing is drawn and the default composite hides the layer
very small Spacing at 4K-ish sizes renders slowly
Wiggle on a static explainer graphic can feel jittery; use Static wiggle

params.name: Mask
params.does: which layer mask is scribbled (mask reference)
params.typical: the mask created by the script

params.name: Fill Type
params.does: fill inside the mask or only along its edge
params.typical: 1 Inside for fills, 2 Center Edge for outlines

params.name: Color
params.does: scribble colour

params.name: Angle
params.does: direction of the scribble strokes in degrees

params.name: Stroke Width
params.does: thickness of each scribble line

params.name: Spacing
params.does: distance between scribble lines

params.name: End
params.does: how much of the scribble is drawn (%), animate for draw-on

params.name: Composite
params.does: draw on the original image, on transparent, or reveal the original through the scribble

cards.scripting: Needs at least one mask on the layer: create the mask first, then point the 'Mask' property at it (mask reference, not settable from a value spec). The 'Scribble' popup (Single Mask / All Masks / All Masks Using Modes in the UI) harvests 5 slots with default 3, so separators may shift indices; verify before setting. Default Composite = 2 (On Transparent) hides the original layer content; set 1 to draw over footage. Opacity is 0-1. Set Random Seed per layer so stacked scribbles differ.

verified.note: status needs_input: needs a mask set by script, so no frame was made

cards.name: Stroke
cards.summary: Paints a brush stroke along a layer mask path, with start/end controls that make it draw on or off like a pen tracing the path.
use_for: circle-the-evidence ring around a face, name or number in news explainers
route line drawing on a map (yatra route, flight path)
underline that draws under a key word or headline
reveal footage along a path (Paint Style = Reveal Original Image)
avoid: without a mask path nothing renders
thin hard strokes look aliased on fast moves; drop Brush Hardness to ~0.75-0.85 and add a touch of glow
for shape-layer work a Trim Paths stroke is cleaner and scales better

params.name: Path
params.does: which mask the stroke follows (mask reference)
params.typical: the mask created by the script

params.name: All Masks
params.does: stroke every mask on the layer instead of one

params.name: Color
params.does: stroke colour

params.name: Brush Size
params.does: stroke thickness in pixels

params.name: Brush Hardness
params.does: edge softness (0-0.95)

params.name: Start
params.does: where along the path the stroke begins (%)

params.name: End
params.does: where along the path the stroke ends (%), animate for draw-on

params.name: Paint Style
params.does: draw on the original image, on transparent, or reveal the original through the stroke

cards.scripting: Requires a mask on the layer: add the mask (closed ellipse for a circle callout, open path for a route) before applying, then set 'Path' to it (mask reference, not settable from a value spec). Opacity is 0-1; Brush Hardness max 0.95. Spacing is the interval between brush dabs (%); high values break the line into separate dots, keep the default 15 or lower. Keyframe End (and optionally Start) for draw-on / draw-off.

verified.note: status needs_input: needs a mask set by script, so no frame was made

cards.name: Vegas
cards.summary: Traces glowing line segments along the outlines found in an image (or along a mask path) and can run them around the contour like chasing marquee lights.
use_for: animated neon outline around a logo or title text
energy / power outline tracing a leader cut-out in a political promo
chasing light border around a lower-third box or map region
tech-style edge trace in AI explainer graphics
avoid: on busy live-action frames Image Contours finds hundreds of tiny noisy contours; pre-blur or use a mask path
contours re-detected each frame flicker on moving footage
thin default yellow stroke looks cheap without glow

params.name: Stroke
params.does: trace source: 1 Image Contours, 2 Mask/Path
params.typical: 1 for logos/text, 2 for a drawn path

params.name: Threshold
params.does: brightness level (0-255) where contours are found

params.name: Pre-Blur
params.does: blurs the input before tracing to drop small noisy contours

params.name: Segments
params.does: number of lit segments per contour
params.typical: 1 for a single comet, 16-40 for marquee

params.name: Length
params.does: fraction of the contour covered by segments (1 = solid outline)

params.name: Rotation
params.does: offsets segments along the contour in degrees; animate to make them travel

params.name: Width
params.does: stroke width in pixels

params.name: Color
params.does: segment colour

cards.scripting: Input Layer is a layer reference (not settable from a value spec); left at None (0) the effect traces the layer it is applied to (believed behaviour, verify). Mask/Path mode (Stroke = 2) needs a mask and the 'Path' mask reference set. Channel: 1 Intensity (default), 2 Red, 3 Green, 4 Blue, 5 Alpha, 6 Hue, 7 Lightness, 8 Saturation, 9 Value (read from After Effects 26.0). End Opacity defaults to 0, so segments fade along their length; set Start/End Opacity 1 for solid segments. Blend Mode 1 (Transparent) shows only the strokes, useful on a duplicate layer for glow passes. Animate Rotation for chasing lights; set Random Phase 1 to desync multiple contours. Never set 'Segments' from a value spec: the 'Segments' group header sits before the 'Segments' slider, so a by-name lookup (ae_lib child()) gets the header, and writing to it killed the AE build (gallery 2026-10-04, no aep saved); leave it at the default 32 or address the slider by index.

verified.note: The old render failed to build (no aep, no frame); with the 'Segments' key dropped it now renders thick yellow dashed marquee segments tracing the contours of the figures, stripes, foreground blocks and flowers over the photo, with some small noisy contours in the background exactly as the avoid notes warn.
verified.second_opinion: corrected: the build died before the aep was saved, which Input Layer = None cannot cause (it only affects the rendered image); the culprit is the 'Segments' demo key, which resolves to the 'Segments' group header (it precedes the slider; Vegas is the only AE effect with such a key and the only one in failed.json). Dropped 'Segments' from demo_settings (default 32), status back to current, scripting note fixed. Re-render needs 'APC Vegas' removed from gallery/ae/failed.json.

cards.name: Write-on
cards.summary: Paints brush dabs at the keyframed Brush Position over time, so an animated position leaves a hand-written / drawn stroke trail on the layer.
use_for: hand-drawn circle or tick around a person or number in a news explainer
signature or handwritten word reveal in documentary titles
drawing a route on a map by keyframing the brush along it
reveal footage through a painted stroke (Paint Style = Reveal Original Image)
avoid: needs many Brush Position keyframes; with a static position it only paints a dot
sparse keyframes give polygonal, mechanical strokes; for clean paths a masked Stroke is easier
Brush Spacing too large leaves visible dot gaps

params.name: Brush Position
params.does: where the brush is at each moment (layer pixels); keyframe it to draw

params.name: Color
params.does: paint colour

params.name: Brush Size
params.does: brush diameter in pixels

params.name: Brush Hardness
params.does: edge softness (0-0.95)

params.name: Stroke Length (secs)
params.does: how long each dab stays visible (0 = forever)
params.typical: 0 for draw-on, 0.3-1 for a comet tail

params.name: Brush Spacing (secs)
params.does: time between dabs; smaller = smoother line

params.name: Paint Style
params.does: paint on the original, on transparent, or reveal the original through the stroke

cards.scripting: The stroke only exists where Brush Position was keyframed in time: generate dense keyframes (every 1-2 frames) from the desired path, e.g. points sampled from a circle or a map route; a common manual trick is pasting a mask path into Brush Position. A static demo shows a single dab. Brush Opacity is 0-1. Paint Time Properties: 1 None, 2 Opacity, 3 Color (default); Brush Time Properties: 1 None (default), 2 Size, 3 Hardness, 4 Size & Hardness (read from After Effects 26.0); leave defaults. No Premiere equivalent: Write-on is absent from the harvested Premiere 2026 video-effect list.

verified.note: A single solid red brush dab sits at frame centre over the untouched footage, exactly what the card says a static Brush Position paints.

cards.name: VR Blur
cards.summary: Blurs 360-degree (equirectangular) footage without leaving a visible seam at the left/right edges or pinching at the poles; on flat footage it still blurs, but treats the frame as a sphere, so the top and bottom smear more sideways than the centre.
use_for: blur 360/VR footage for a background or title plate
seamless blur-in / blur-out transition on 360 clips
soft background behind text in VR explainers
avoid: on normal 16:9 footage use Gaussian Blur or Camera Lens Blur instead; this one assumes a sphere and is slower
wrong Frame Layout on stereo footage blurs across the two eyes
Software-only (CPU) renders: it draws only a dark-red 'This effect requires GPU acceleration' slate

params.name: Blurriness
params.does: blur amount

params.name: Frame Layout
params.does: mono, stereo over/under or stereo side-by-side 360 layout

params.name: Auto VR Properties
params.does: read layout and field of view from the comp automatically

params.name: Horizontal Field of View
params.does: horizontal FOV the frame covers in degrees

params.name: Vertical Field of View
params.does: vertical FOV the frame covers in degrees

cards.scripting: Only meaningful on 2:1 equirectangular 360 footage; set Auto VR Properties = 1 or set the FOVs to match the source. Frame Layout labels are approximate (mono / stereo over-under / stereo side-by-side). Needs GPU acceleration (verified 2026-10-13): a software-only (Mercury Software Only) aerender draws a dark-red 'This effect requires GPU acceleration' slate instead of the image, a CUDA render draws the effect; set the project renderer to GPU (app.project.gpuAccelType, vfx.render_scenes(gpu=True), gallery.py --gpu) before building or rendering. The renderer a project is set to also becomes After Effects' default for new projects.

verified.note: GPU render: the whole frame is evenly blurred, with a thin horizontally smeared band along the top and bottom edges.
verified.recheck: 2026-10-13: re-rendered in live wave 1 (frames the old verdict was judged on: pve/work/gallery_pre_fix/)

cards.name: VR Chromatic Aberrations
cards.summary: Offsets the red, green and blue channels outward from a point of interest with a falloff, giving colour fringing that is seam-aware for 360 footage.
use_for: lens-imperfection realism on 360 footage
RGB-split hit on a beat or transition (keyframe the aberration)
edgy tech / glitch accent in AI explainers
avoid: on normal footage a dedicated RGB split / channel offset is lighter and more controllable
large values on faces or text make them unreadable
constant heavy fringing looks cheap; use as a short hit
Software-only (CPU) renders: it draws only a dark-red 'This effect requires GPU acceleration' slate

params.name: Aberration (Red)
params.does: red channel offset (signed)

params.name: Aberration (Green)
params.does: green channel offset (signed)

params.name: Aberration (Blue)
params.does: blue channel offset (signed)

params.name: Point of Interest
params.does: centre around which the frame stays clean (layer pixels)

params.name: Falloff Distance
params.does: how far from the point of interest the fringing builds up

params.name: Falloff Invert
params.does: flip the falloff so the centre is affected instead of the edges

params.name: Frame Layout
params.does: mono / stereo 360 layout

cards.scripting: Point of Interest is in layer pixels. Exact meaning/direction of Falloff Distance (0-100) is not verified; check a frame. Built for 360 equirectangular footage (set Auto VR Properties = 1 in a 2:1 comp); on flat footage it still splits channels. Needs GPU acceleration (verified 2026-10-13): a software-only (Mercury Software Only) aerender draws a dark-red 'This effect requires GPU acceleration' slate instead of the image, a CUDA render draws the effect; set the project renderer to GPU (app.project.gpuAccelType, vfx.render_scenes(gpu=True), gallery.py --gpu) before building or rendering. The renderer a project is set to also becomes After Effects' default for new projects.

cards.name: VR Color Gradients
cards.summary: Overlays a soft multi-point colour gradient (up to 8 coloured points) on the footage with a chosen blend mode and opacity, wrapped correctly for 360 footage.
use_for: mood tint / colour wash on 360 footage
teal-orange or brand-colour gradient over a title background
soft light-leak style wash in reels and trailers
avoid: at the default 100% Opacity and default blend mode the gradient covers the footage almost entirely; drop Opacity
default 8 points include black and white and produce a muddy rainbow; reduce Points Number
on flat footage 4-Color Gradient is simpler
Software-only (CPU) renders: it draws only a dark-red 'This effect requires GPU acceleration' slate

params.name: Points Number
params.does: how many colour points are used (1-8)

params.name: Point 1
params.does: position of colour point 1 (layer pixels); Point 2..8 likewise

params.name: Color 1
params.does: colour of point 1; Color 2..8 likewise

params.name: Gradient Power
params.does: how strongly each point dominates its area

params.name: Gradient Blend
params.does: smoothness of transitions between points

params.name: Opacity
params.does: overall strength of the overlay in %

params.name: Blending Mode
params.does: how the gradient composites (1-based popup, 22 slots)

cards.scripting: Points are in layer pixels; only the first 'Points Number' points are used. Blending Mode is a 22-slot popup (1 None, 2 Normal (default), 4 Add, 5 Multiply, 6 Screen ...; enum_labels (read from After Effects 26.0)); keep the default and control strength with Opacity. The renderer a project is set to also becomes After Effects' default for new projects.

cards.name: VR Converter
cards.summary: Re-projects footage between 360 formats (equirectangular, cube-map layouts, fisheye and a flat 2D source) and can re-orient the sphere with tilt, pan and roll.
use_for: convert cube-map or fisheye 360 footage to equirectangular for editing
place a flat 2D graphic correctly into a 360 frame
re-orient a 360 shot so the subject faces front
extract a flat view out of 360 footage
avoid: on ordinary 16:9 footage it only produces a meaningless warp
changing Output Frame Width changes the effect's output size, so the layer may no longer fill the comp
Software-only (CPU) renders: it draws only a dark-red 'This effect requires GPU acceleration' slate

params.name: Input
params.does: projection of the source footage (1-based popup, 9 options)

params.name: Output
params.does: projection to produce (1-based popup, 8 options)

params.name: Output Frame Width
params.does: pixel width of the converted output

params.name: FOV
params.does: field of view in degrees used for 2D/fisheye sources

params.name: Pan (Y axis)
params.does: rotates the sphere left/right in degrees

params.name: Tilt (X axis)
params.does: rotates the sphere up/down in degrees

params.name: Roll (Z axis)
params.does: rolls the horizon in degrees

cards.scripting: Input (read from After Effects 26.0): 1 2D Source, 2 Cube-map 4:3, 3 Sphere-map, 4 Equirectangular 2:1, 5 Fisheye (FullDome), 6 Cube-map Facebook 3:2, 7 Cube-map Pano2VR 3:2, 8 Cube-map GearVR 6:1, 9 Equirectangular 16:9; Output is the same list without 2D Source (1 Cube-map 4:3 ... 3 Equirectangular 2:1 ... 8 Equirectangular 16:9). Defaults (Input 1, Output 3) produce a visible re-projection on a flat frame. Output Frame Width (256-16384) resizes the effect output; put the layer in a precomp sized to the target projection (2:1 for equirectangular). No AE-to-Premiere one-to-one: Premiere's VR Projection covers re-orientation and 2D-to-360 placement only. Needs GPU acceleration (verified 2026-10-13): a software-only (Mercury Software Only) aerender draws a dark-red 'This effect requires GPU acceleration' slate instead of the image, a CUDA render draws the effect; set the project renderer to GPU (app.project.gpuAccelType, vfx.render_scenes(gpu=True), gallery.py --gpu) before building or rendering. The renderer a project is set to also becomes After Effects' default for new projects.
